subject: Marine mammal distance sampling survey - replication/increasing

messages.author: 09fc2b0bc75dcccf
messages.subject: Marine mammal distance sampling survey - replication/increasing
parts:
Hi all,

I was hoping for some feedback re increasing the number of transects for =
a marine mammal survey.

My study area is ~75 km by 40 km. The transects will be spaced 6 km apart=
(based on previous research indicating a truncation distance of ~2-3 km =
for humpback whales). Thus, the maximum number of transects I can fit in =
my study area in one survey pass is 12 transects. However, distance sampl=
ing literature states it is best to have at least 20 transects.

Can I increase the number of transects by using Distance to create a surv=
ey design that randomly places transects 6km apart, and repeating this pr=
ocess 3 times? i.e. within one season, survey the study area 3 complete t=
imes using three different sets of randomly placed transects, resulting i=
n a sample size of 36 transects?
Or, generating a survey design with randomly placed transects in Distance=
once, and for the subsequent two survey passes, offsetting the transects=
by 2km each?

Which option is best? Three random survey designs or three survey passes =
of transects offset by 2km from the original random survey design (to inc=
rease survey coverage of the study area)?
Can these data then be analyzed as 36 independent samples?

This survey will be conducted each season over 1 year (4 seasons of data =
total). I was planning on surveying the same transects across seasons and=
potentially pooling the data as suggested in previous posts (i.e. sample=
size is 36, and length =3D line length x number of visits).
I hope this makes sense and any feedback would be much appreciated.

Please reply to my e-mail address below; I will summarize the ensuing dis=
cussion
to the list.

Thanks, Elaine Leung
elaine...@gmail.com
